jobs.run.py: This job runs the foraging-cell model (a validation check, the three-way comparison, or a rendering); its comparison of particle, continuum and closed-form descriptions shows which microscopic response rule a population measurement can identify.
jobs.generate_figure_1_response_rules.py: This job draws the nine elementary rules by which a cell can change its swimming in response to nutrient, so readers see the candidate strategies before they are compared.
jobs.generate_figure_2_nutrient_landscape.py: This job draws the single-wavelength nutrient landscape and computes the design numbers behind it, because every closed-form prediction in the paper depends on that one wavenumber.
jobs.generate_figure_4_macroscopic_observable: This job runs the same population release three ways (particle walk, continuum equation, closed-form prediction) and plots their large-scale observables, so agreement between the three descriptions can be checked.
jobs.generate_figure_5_foraging_observables.p: This job measures how much nutrient each response rule gains over time relative to its predicted gain, showing what a population actually earns from each foraging strategy.
jobs.generate_figure_6_information_observable: This job measures how well each response rule steers cells along the nutrient gradient after a time lag, showing how much navigational information the population carries.
jobs.check_numerical_convergence.py: This job reruns the simulations with smaller time steps and finer grids to show that the reported results do not depend on numerical resolution.
jobs.check_sampling_floor.py: This job separates random sampling noise from systematic error of the continuum closure, so a mismatch is attributed to the right cause.
jobs.benchmark_performance.py: This job times a small version of the particle pipeline at several thread counts and batch sizes, so production runs use measured rather than guessed settings.
jobs.generate_manuscript_videos.py: This job renders the two supplementary videos from the saved comparison archives so readers can watch the density evolve in time.
